questions.q: Why does the health check script check the instance's restart time before its wait stats section?
options: Because a fresh restart resets wait stats and the plan cache, which changes how the rest of the output should be interpreted
Because SQL Server requires SERVERPROPERTY to run before any other query
Restart time has no bearing on interpreting wait stats
To confirm the server is actually turned on
questions.explain: Wait stats accumulate since the last restart — a server that just restarted has only a few minutes of wait data, not a representative picture.

questions.q: Which DMV does the health check script use to find when the instance last started?
options: sys.dm_os_sys_info
sys.dm_exec_requests
sys.dm_os_wait_stats
sys.database_files
questions.explain: sys.dm_os_sys_info exposes sqlserver_start_time, used to calculate hours since the last restart.

questions.q: What does the database space section's benign-wait-free FILEPROPERTY(name, 'SpaceUsed') calculation depend on?
options: Running the query in the context of the target database (USE first)
Running the query only against tempdb
Running the query with sysadmin permissions on a different server
It works identically regardless of database context
questions.explain: sys.database_files and FILEPROPERTY both operate on the current database context, so the file-space section must be run inside the database being checked.

questions.q: Why is a small fixed-MB autogrowth setting flagged as worth noticing on a large, active database?
options: Because file growth events pause writes, and a small fixed increment on a large active file means those pauses happen very frequently
Because fixed-MB growth settings are not supported in modern SQL Server versions
Because it means the database will never run out of space
Because percent-based growth is always slower than fixed-MB growth
questions.explain: A small fixed growth increment means the file needs to autogrow far more often as it fills, and each growth event briefly pauses writes to that file.

questions.q: In the health check script's wait stats section, what is the purpose of the benign-wait exclusion list?
options: It filters out normal background housekeeping waits so the waits that actually explain slowness stand out
It hides all wait types with fewer than 10 waiting tasks
It removes waits related to backup and restore operations only
It is required syntax for querying sys.dm_os_wait_stats
questions.explain: Without excluding benign waits like SLEEP_TASK and LAZYWRITER_SLEEP, they crowd out the wait types that actually indicate a problem.
